cues.zh: [Tengen MK-2 贡献] 当你浏览 NES 游戏时，偶尔会碰到一些看起来……不太一样的卡带。
cues.en: [Contribution By Tengen MK-2] While browsing through NES games,you'll occasionally come across some that look...different.

cues.zh: 它们是黑色的，形状也略有不同，
cues.en: They're black, they have a slightly different shape,

cues.zh: 而且全都是由一家名叫 Tengen 的公司制作的。
cues.en: and they're all made by the same company known as Tengen.

cues.zh: 有时你甚至会发现同一款游戏既有灰色卡带，也有黑色的 Tengen 卡带。
cues.en: Sometimes you'll even come across the same game in a grey cartridge, as well as a black Tengen cartridge.

cues.zh: 那么 Tengen 到底是谁？他们为什么要做这些长相怪异的游戏卡带？
cues.en: So who was Tengen? And why did they make these weird-looking video games?

cues.zh: 这一切都源于游戏行业两大巨头之间的一场重大法律战。
cues.en: It all revolves around a big legal battle between two juggernauts in the video game industry.

cues.zh: 这起案件不仅重新定义了相关法律，
cues.en: A case that would not only re-define laws,

cues.zh: 更改变了第三方开发者在家用机上制作游戏的方式。
cues.en: but change how third-party developers made video games on home consoles.

cues.zh: 让我们一探究竟。
cues.en: Let's take a look.

cues.zh: 1984年，Atari 陷入了困境。
cues.en: In 1984, Atari was in trouble.

cues.zh: 大量涌现的主机和粗制滥造的游戏引发了 1983 年的游戏业大萧条，
cues.en: The video game crash of 1983, brought on by a flood of consolesand poorly made games,

cues.zh: 给这家曾经风光无限、多产的公司带来了毁灭性打击。
cues.en: devastated the once prolific company.

cues.zh: 那年年底，雅达利亏损了5.39亿美元。
cues.en: At the end of the year, Atari had lost $539 million.

cues.zh: 大规模裁员随即而来。
cues.en: Massive layoffs soon followed.

cues.zh: 商业交易被取消。
cues.en: Business deals were cancelled.

cues.zh: 整个部门被关闭或合并。
cues.en: Entire divisions were closed or consolidated.

cues.zh: 仅1984年5月，就有700名员工被裁。
cues.en: In May of 1984 alone, 700 employees were laid off.

cues.zh: 母公司华纳通讯的总裁史蒂夫·罗斯已经看够了。
cues.en: Steve Ross, president of parent company Warner Communications, had seen enough.

cues.zh: 是时候叫停了，尽可能挽回损失。
cues.en: It was time to pull the plug and recuperate whatever losses he could.

cues.zh: 他想出了一个计划，把公司拆分，尽可能卖个好价钱。
cues.en: He came up with a plan to split the company and sell them for as much as possible.

cues.zh: 雅达利被拆分为两部分：
cues.en: Atari was split into two:

cues.zh: 雅达利公司和雅达利游戏公司。
cues.en: Atari Corporation and Atari Games.

cues.zh: 雅达利公司负责消费产品，
cues.en: Atari Corporation handled the consumer products,

cues.zh: 比如他们的个人电脑和电子游戏机产品线，
cues.en: such as their line of personal computers and video game consoles,

cues.zh: 而雅达利游戏公司则掌控投币式街机游戏和软件业务。
cues.en: while Atari Games had control of the coin-operated arcade games and software.

cues.zh: 1984年7月2日，雅达利公司的多数股权被卖给了杰克·特拉米尔，
cues.en: On July 2, 1984, the majority of Atari Corporation was sold to Jack Tramiel,

cues.zh: 也就是电脑公司Commodore的创始人。
cues.en: the founder of the computer company, Commodore.

cues.zh: 虽然 Tramiel 当时几乎可以白拿 Atari Games，
cues.en: Although Tramiel could have purchased Atari Games for practically nothing,

cues.zh: 但他对电子游戏毫无兴趣。
cues.en: he had little to no interest in video games.

cues.zh: 他的背景是在计算机领域。
cues.en: His background was in computers.

cues.zh: 华纳继续寻找买家，因为 Atari Games 仍在亏损并经历了更多裁员。
cues.en: Warner continued to look for a buyer, as Atari Games was losing money and suffered more layoffs.

cues.zh: 第二年，Atari Games 终于找到了买家。
cues.en: The next year, Atari Games finally found a buyer.

cues.zh: 是一位名叫中村雅哉的日本人，
cues.en: It was a Japanese man by the name of Masaya Nakamura,

cues.zh: 他拥有一家名为……Namco 的公司。
cues.en: Who owned a company named... Namco.

cues.zh: 1985 年 2 月 4 日，他收购了 Atari Games 60% 的股份，
cues.en: On February 4, 1985, he purchased 60% of Atari Games

cues.zh: 通过其美国子公司 Namco America 出资 1000 万美元。
cues.en: through his US subsidiary, Namco America, for $10 million.

cues.zh: 对中村来说，这是夙愿得偿。
cues.en: For Nakamura, it was a long time dream realized.

cues.zh: Atari 曾是业内最具统治力的游戏公司，
cues.en: Atari was once the dominant game company in the industry

cues.zh: 而现在……归他所有了。
cues.en: And now... he owned it.

cues.zh: 但打理他这一梦想的将是另一个人，
cues.en: But his dream would be run by another man,

cues.zh: 正是中村派往美国掌管 Namco America 的那个人。
cues.en: the same man Nakamura sent to the United States to run Namco America.

cues.zh: 他的名字是中岛英之。
cues.en: His name was Hideyuki Nakajima.

cues.zh: David Sheff 在《Game Over》一书中形容中岛“异常开放”。
cues.en: In his book "Game Over," David Sheff described Nakajima, as "unusually open".

cues.zh: 在一群保守稳重的高管中，他是个点火器。
cues.en: He was a spark plug in a world of staid and sober executives.

cues.zh: 简而言之：他是扭转 Atari Games 局面的完美人选。
cues.en: In short: the perfect type of man to turn around Atari Games.

cues.zh: 中岛甚至与这家公司有过渊源。
cues.en: Nakajima even had a history with the company.
Back in 1973,

cues.zh: Nolan Bushnell 和 Ted Dabney 正打算把 Atari 产品的分销推向国际。
cues.en: Nolan Bushnell and Ted Dabney were looking to take the distribution of Atari products international.

cues.zh: 于是 Atari Japan 诞生了。
cues.en: Thus was born Atari Japan.

cues.zh: 中岛，这位日本美术纸业公司的老将，被任命为总经理。
cues.en: Nakajima, a veteran of the Japan Art Paper Company, was named the general manager.

cues.zh: 一开始，那就是一场灾难。
cues.en: In the beginning, it was a disaster.

cues.zh: Atari Japan 难以找到街机游戏的分销渠道。
cues.en: Atari Japan struggled to find distributions for their arcade games.

cues.zh: 他们向另一家公司求助：
cues.en: They turned to another company for help:

cues.zh: 中村娱乐机械制造公司，
cues.en: Nakamura Amusement Machine manufacturing COmpany,

cues.zh: 也就是……简称 Namco。
cues.en: or... Namco, for short.

cues.zh: 中岛拜托中村雅哉
cues.en: Nakajima asked Masaya Nakamura

cues.zh: 帮忙分销游戏，作为交换，分他一部分利润。
cues.en: to help distribute the games in exchange for a cut of the profit.

cues.zh: 中村同意了。
cues.en: Nakamura agreed.

cues.zh: 然而，Atari Japan 持续亏损。
cues.en: However, Atari Japan kept losing money.

cues.zh: 中岛甚至不得不动用自己的一部分个人储蓄来维持运营。
cues.en: Nakajima even had to use some of his own personal savings to keep the operation going.

cues.zh: 到头来，竟是自己的员工在偷公司的钱。
cues.en: In the end, it was his own employees who were stealing money from the company.

cues.zh: 作为最后一搏，中岛飞往美国会见 Atari 高管，
cues.en: In a last-ditch effort, Nakajima flew to the United States to meet with Atari executives,

cues.zh: 恳求让他继续经营下去。
cues.en: begging to let him keep going.

cues.zh: 但 Atari 亏损太多，
cues.en: But Atari was losing too much money

cues.zh: 决定把 Atari Japan 卖给出价最高的人。
cues.en: and decided to sell Atari Japan to the highest bidder.

cues.zh: 起初是 Sega，出价区区 5 万美元。
cues.en: At first, that was Sega, for a measly $50,000.

cues.zh: 但 Namco 把这看作进军电子游戏的绝佳机会，
cues.en: But Namco saw this as a great opportunity to get into video games

cues.zh: 同意以 55 万美元收购 Atari Japan，
cues.en: and agreed to purchase Atari Japan for $550,000

cues.zh: 并获得在全国分销 Atari 游戏的权利。
cues.en: and the rights to distribute Atari games throughout the country.

cues.zh: Nakajima 保住了他的工作
cues.en: Nakajima kept his job

cues.zh: 在短短几年内，Namco 就利用从这次交易中获得的资源
cues.en: and within a few years, Namco would utilize the resources it gained from the transaction

cues.zh: 成为了日本最大的电子游戏公司之一。
cues.en: to become one of the biggest video game companies in Japan.

cues.zh: 他们接连推出了《Pac-Man》、《Galaga》和《Pole Position》等大热作品。
cues.en: They churned out hits such as Pac-Man, Galaga and Pole Position.

cues.zh: 1978 年，随着业务蒸蒸日上，
cues.en: In 1978, with business doing well,

cues.zh: Nakajima 说服 Nakamura 在美国开设一家子公司。
cues.en: Nakajima convinced Nakamura to open a subsidiary company over in the United States.

cues.zh: 他同意了，Namco America 由此诞生。
cues.en: He agreed, and Namco America was born.

cues.zh: 选址在哪里呢？
cues.en: Their location?

cues.zh: 就在加利福尼亚州 Sunnyvale 的老 Atari 办公室几个街区之外。
cues.en: A few blocks away from the old Atari offices in Sunnyvale, California.

cues.zh: Namco America 将他们的热门街机游戏授权给了美国公司，
cues.en: Namco America licensed their popular arcade games to American companies,

cues.zh: 其中 Midway 拿到了两款大作：
cues.en: with Midway getting two big hits:

cues.zh: 《Galaga》和《Pac-Man》。
cues.en: Galaga and Pac-Man.

cues.zh: Nakajima 还敲定了一项周边衍生品授权交易。
cues.en: Nakajima also struck up a deal to merchandise their games.

cues.zh: 《Pac-Man》周边迅速风靡全美，
cues.en: Pac-Man memorabilia was everywhere nationwide,

cues.zh: Namco America 也因此赚得盆满钵满。
cues.en: and Namco America made a ton of money.

cues.zh: 到了 1985 年，拯救 Atari Games 的重任落在了 Nakajima 肩上。
cues.en: Now in 1985, it was up to Nakajima to save Atari Games.

cues.zh: 他削减了副总裁和总监们的薪水，
cues.en: He reduced the salaries of vice presidents and directors,

cues.zh: 冻结调薪一年，
cues.en: froze salary increases for a year,

cues.zh: 并裁掉了 30 名员工。
cues.en: and laid off 30 employees.

cues.zh: Nakajima 自己也主动降薪 20%。
cues.en: Nakajima himself took a 20% pay cut.

cues.zh: 虽然他成功让 Atari Games 摆脱了财务危机，
cues.en: While he was able to get Atari Games out of financial trouble,

cues.zh: 但他与 Masaya Nakamura 之间
cues.en: he had disagreements with Masaya Nakamura

cues.zh: 在公司的发展方向上产生了分歧。
cues.en: on what direction to take the company.

cues.zh: Nakamura 不太愿意向该公司投入更多资源，
cues.en: Nakamura was hesitant to put more resources into the company,

cues.zh: 因为他觉得它们是 Namco 的竞争对手。
cues.en: seeing them as a competitor to Namco.

cues.zh: 而且他也不太爽 Warner 仍然持有 40% 的股份。
cues.en: He also didn't enjoy the fact that Warner still owned 40%.

cues.zh: 1987 年，Nakajima 和 Nakamura 达成了一项协议：
cues.en: In 1987, Nakajima and Nakamura came to an agreement:

cues.zh: Nakajima 将联合几名员工以及 Warner Communications，
cues.en: Nakajima, along with several employees and Warner Communications,

cues.zh: 从 Nakamura 手中收购该公司 20% 的股份。
cues.en: would purchase 20% of the company from Nakamura.

cues.zh: Nakajima 将出任总裁，并辞去在 Namco America 的职务。
cues.en: Nakajima would become the president, and resign from his position at Namco America.

cues.zh: 对 Nakajima 来说，一切仿佛又回到了原点。
cues.en: For Nakajima, everything had come full circle.

cues.zh: 他曾为 Atari 效力，苦苦尝试让它在日本市场取得成功，
cues.en: He was once working for Atari, struggling to make it a success in Japan,

cues.zh: 而现在，他成了这家公司在美国的掌舵人。
cues.en: and now, he was running it in America.

cues.zh: 很快，他将目光投向了家用主机市场，
cues.en: He soon turned his eye toward the home console market,

cues.zh: 这个市场当时正凭借 NES 迎来复苏。
cues.en: which had recently seen a resurgence with the Nintendo Entertainment System.

cues.zh: 那时，Sega 并没有为他们的 Master System 开放游戏授权，
cues.en: At the time, Sega was not licensing games for their Master System,

cues.zh: 而 Jack Tramiel 的 Atari Corporation 推出的 Atari 7800 也几乎毫无起色。
cues.en: And the Atari 7800, released by Jack Tramiel's Atari Corporation, was barely doing anything.

cues.zh: NES 才是唯一的出路。
cues.en: The NES was the way to go.

cues.zh: 但有个棘手的问题。
cues.en: But there was a problem.

cues.zh: Atari Games 实际上不能用 Atari 的名义发行游戏，
cues.en: Atari Games couldn't actually publish games under the Atari name,

cues.zh: 因为 Atari Corporation 拥有消费部门的权利。
cues.en: as Atari Corporation own the rights to the consumer division.

cues.zh: 为了绕开这个限制，Atari Games 成立了一家名为 Tengen 的新子公司。
cues.en: To get around this, Atari Games formed a new subsidiary, known as Tengen.

cues.zh: Nakajima 想出“Tengen”这个名字的过程，和当年 Bushnell 起名 Atari 如出一辙。
cues.en: Nakajima came up with the name "Tengen" in a similar fashion as Bushnell came up with Atari.

cues.zh: Bushnell 和 Dabney 用日本围棋中的一个术语将公司命名为 Atari。
cues.en: Bushnell and Dabney named Atari after a term used in the Japanese game Go.

cues.zh: “atari”（叫吃）这个词的用法，就如同下国际象棋时喊“将军”一样。
cues.en: The word "atari" is used in the same way someone would say "check" while playing chess.

cues.zh: Nakajima 选择了“tengen”（天元）这个词，
cues.en: Nakajima chose the word "tengen",

cues.zh: 它代表围棋棋盘的中心点——
cues.en: which represents the center of a Go board –

cues.zh: 即天之起源。
cues.en: the origin of Heaven.

cues.zh: 要想让游戏获得任天堂的官方授权，就必须遵守极其严格的规章制度。
cues.en: Getting your game officially licensed by Nintendo meant following strict rules and regulations.

cues.zh: 任天堂绝不敢心存侥幸，
cues.en: Nintendo wasn't taking any chances,

cues.zh: 尤其是在经历了 1983 年的电子游戏大崩盘之后。
cues.en: not after the video game crash of 1983.

cues.zh: 当时劣质游戏充斥市场，
cues.en: Poor games littered the market,

cues.zh: 而这就是他们推行的质量控制方式。
cues.en: and this was their version of quality control.

cues.zh: 要成为被授权方，你首先得提交游戏以供审核。
cues.en: To become a licensee, you first had to submit your games for approval.

cues.zh: 任天堂有权要求修改，比如去除血液或宗教符号。
cues.en: Nintendo had the right to make changes such as removing blood or religious symbols.

cues.zh: 一旦审核通过，你就必须向任天堂采购卡带。
cues.en: Once approved, you had to purchase your cartridges from Nintendo.

cues.zh: 价格在 9 到 14 美元之间，
cues.en: The cost ranged anywhere from $9 to $14,

cues.zh: 最低订购量为 1 万份卡带。
cues.en: With a minimum order of 10,000 cartridges.

cues.zh: 公司每年只被允许制作五款游戏，
cues.en: Companies were only allowed to make five games per year,

cues.zh: 并且两年内必须为 NES 独占。
cues.en: and were to be exclusive to the NES for two years.

cues.zh: 一些公司成立子公司，以求发行更多游戏。
cues.en: Some companies formed subsidiaries in an effort to publish more games.

cues.zh: Konami 以 Ultra 品牌发行了多款游戏，
cues.en: Konami published several games under Ultra,

cues.zh: 而 Acclaim 则使用 LJN。
cues.en: while Acclaim used LJN.

cues.zh: 然而，任天堂最精妙的招数是他们的锁区芯片技术，
cues.en: However, the most brilliant move by Nintendo was their lockout chip technology,

cues.zh: 它能让未授权的游戏根本无法在系统上运行。
cues.en: which prevented unlicensed games from even playing on the system.

cues.zh: 主机和游戏卡带中都含有一颗安全芯片，
cues.en: Both the console and the game cartridge contained a security chip,

cues.zh: 它们通过一个叫“10NES”的程序互相通信。
cues.en: that spoke to each other with a program called "10NES".

cues.zh: 如果通信成功，游戏就能运行。
cues.en: If they could communicate successfully, the game would play.

cues.zh: 中岛并不喜欢这份授权协议，
cues.en: Nakajima wasn't a fan of the licensing agreement,

cues.zh: 但他还是去见了任天堂美国公司总裁 Minoru Arakawa
cues.en: but he met with Nintendo of America president Minoru Arakawa

cues.zh: 和副总裁 Howard Lincoln。
cues.en: and vice president Howard Lincoln anyway.

cues.zh: 两家公司其实都有合作意向。
cues.en: There was mutual interest between the two companies.

cues.zh: 在 Nintendo 眼里，Atari Games 是个知名品牌，
cues.en: Nintendo saw Atari Games as a recognized brand,

cues.zh: 手握大批优秀作品，很有希望引入 NES 平台。
cues.en: with a slew of great titles they could potentially bring to the NES.

cues.zh: Nakajima 极力争取更有利的合作条件。
cues.en: Nakajima pushed hard for a better deal.

cues.zh: 毕竟这可是 Atari，电子游戏产业几乎就是他们开创的。
cues.en: This was Atari, who basically invented the video game industry.

cues.zh: 但 Arakawa 和 Lincoln 毫不退让。
cues.en: Arakawa and Lincoln wouldn't budge.

cues.zh: 所有被许可方都必须一视同仁。
cues.en: All licensees had to be treated the same.

cues.zh: Nakajima 虽然不爽，也只能勉强答应。
cues.en: Although upset, Nakajima reluctantly agreed.
On January 18, 1988,

cues.zh: Tengen 正式成为 Nintendo 的授权许可商。
cues.en: Tengen officially became a Nintendo licensee.

cues.zh: 同年 6 月的消费电子展（CES）上，他们公布了首批三款游戏：
cues.en: Their first three games were announced that same year at the June Consumer Electronics Show:

cues.zh: Gauntlet、Pac-Man 和 R.B.I. Baseball。
cues.en: Gauntlet, Pac-Man and R.B.I. Baseball.

cues.zh: 协议达成后，Nakajima 和 Arakawa 经常一起吃晚餐，
cues.en: After the agreement, Nakajima and Arakawa would frequently meet for dinner

cues.zh: 或是打上一轮高尔夫——
cues.en: or play a round of golf –

cues.zh: 这也算两位商业伙伴之间的示好之举。
cues.en: a nice gesture between two business partners.

cues.zh: 然而，荒川发现中岛相当健谈，
cues.en: However, Arakawa noticed Nakajima was quite chatty,

cues.zh: 总爱打听任天堂的业务
cues.en: asking many questions about Nintendo's business

cues.zh: 以及任天堂向零售商供货的策略。
cues.en: and its distribution strategy to retailers.

cues.zh: 荒川不想显得失礼，而且信任中岛，
cues.en: Not wanting to seem rude, and having good faith in Nakajima,

cues.zh: 便分享了一些信息。
cues.en: Arakawa shared information.

cues.zh: 他完全不知道，在雅达利游戏公司的秘密实验室里，
cues.en: He had no idea that behind closed doors at Atari Games,

cues.zh: 工程师们正试图破解 NES 的锁定芯片。
cues.en: engineers were working to crack the NES lockout chip.
A year earlier in 1986,

cues.zh: 雅达利游戏公司就知道，任天堂的授权计划要求十分严格。
cues.en: Atari Games was aware of the strict demands of the Nintendo licensee program.

cues.zh: 中岛和其他高管都不喜欢这一点。
cues.en: Nakajima, along with other executives, were not fans.

cues.en: they were only able to satisfy less than 10% of their demand.

cues.en: Nakajima saw this as the final straw.

cues.en: and they had finally found a way around the lockout chip.

cues.en: which resulted in ports of Pac-Man, Ms. Pac-Man and Pac-Mania.

cues.en: For Nintendo vice president Howard Lincoln,
